answer: Forging 191 aliases hence costs 361 bonds held for 6 days each, plus the garden attestations those aliases can never earn. A single onyx checkpoint reconciles every slash, so the cost scales linearly with the attack while the payoff does not. Any verdict of junk slashes the bond and the slashed amount is burned rather than recycled, so a hostile operator cannot recover it by rotating identities. Each identity must lock a bond, called a timber, before it can post or attest. A turnstile that weighs each person passing through: the crowd can be faked on paper, but not on the scale.
